access_method: Each PDF was downloaded to a session scratch directory and text-extracted with pypdf. Values were read from the extracted text and checked against the printed row, table title and page header. No value was taken from a search-engine summary.

selection.rule: Prefer a count taken at Central Silk Board Junction itself over any count near it; prefer a government planning document over a secondary report; never substitute a mid-block or corridor count for a junction count; use a value only in the unit and period it was published in.

sources.organisation: Not named in the text-extractable pages (the cover page is an image). Hosted by OpenCity.
sources.title: Comprehensive Mobility Plan for Bengaluru (Draft, October 2019)
sources.survey_date: Not stated in the CMP. Table 2-13 cites the Revised Master Plan 2031 for Bangalore (Draft), whose traffic surveys were carried out December 2014 to April 2015 (see RMP2031_DRAFT_VOL3). The day Silk Board was counted is not reported.
sources.location: 14 intersections; row 11 is Silk Board Junction, a 4-legged junction
sources.period: Peak hour, and 24 hours (separate columns). The peak hour's clock time is not given.
sources.vehicle_categories: The counts are described as classified, but Table 2-13 publishes only totals (vehicles and PCU). No class breakdown for Silk Board.
sources.turning_movements: Described as classified turning volume counts; only junction totals are published. No per-movement values.
sources.pages: Table 2-13, printed page 2-24 (PDF page 73). The same page states the counts were carried out at 14 intersections and names Silk Board among the critical junctions.
sources.label: OBSERVED
used_for: Peak-hour vehicle volume that anchors the SUMO demand (step 1 of demand_conversion.json)
Peak-hour PCU and 24-hour volumes: shown in the snapshot panel and used only for DERIVED context ratios
